member.name: T:Utilities.Api.Controllers.ProxiesController
member.summary:
Both proxy planes behind one controller:
Control plane (Phase 1 / SPEC3) — a resource-oriented surface rooted at /api/Proxies: the collection itself, one proxy at /{proxyId}, and its /versions, /executions and /overview sub-resources. The controller segment still comes from [controller] plus the global api prefix (); only the sub-paths are explicit. Every action requires a bearer token and the tenant is taken from . Where a service result carries its own HttpStatus the controller honours it, so the service stays the single source of truth for the SPEC §3.4 error contract.
Data plane (Phase 2) — at {METHOD} /api/proxy/gateway/{slug}/{**path}, the path a tenant's client calls instead of the vendor. That route is pinned absolutely rather than derived from the convention, because it is a published contract (see the remarks on ). It is at the framework level because the credential is the X-Blocks-Key header rather than the standard scheme.
A route id always wins over the same id supplied in the body or query string: the URL identifies the resource, the payload only describes it.

member.name: F:Utilities.Api.Controllers.ProxiesController.GatewayHardBodyLimitBytes
member.summary:
Kestrel-level backstop on the gateway body, deliberately ABOVE (10 MB) rather than equal to it.
The 10 MB cap has to stay in application code: exceeding it is a documented outcome (RequestTooLarge) that answers 413 with the Blocks error body and still records an execution row. A framework-level limit set to the same value would pre-empt that and return a bare Kestrel 413 with no row and no code. This one only catches a client streaming far past the point where the answer is already decided, so the contract is unchanged and the ceiling is bounded.
Takes the four control-plane services plus the two data-plane gateway services.

member.name: M:Utilities.Api.Controllers.ProxiesController.Gateway(System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Data plane (Phase 2). A tenant's client calls {METHOD} /api/proxy/gateway/{slug}/{**path} instead of the vendor; Blocks authenticates the caller with the X-Blocks-Key tenant header + a bearer valid for that tenant, rebuilds the request against the stored upstream, attaches ONLY the configured headers / query params, calls the third party server-side, relays the response, and records one per attempt.
Unlike the control-plane actions above, this route is pinned absolutely (~/) instead of being derived from [controller]. The path is a published contract that third-party clients hard-code, so it must not change if this method or its controller is ever renamed, and the registered template must be the exact lowercase spelling we document rather than a case-insensitive match for it. The leading ~/ also makes it skip , so the api segment is written here once and never doubled.

member.summary: Relays the upstream status, body, and Content-Type byte-for-byte. No other header is relayed.
